reference: The runner validation report shows no util-linux blkid executable in its allowed reference PATH, so this suite makes no util-linux parity claim. Runnable probe cases are documented-contract checks: small Bash-printf encoders write ext superblock UUID/label/type fields, FAT BPB serial/label/type fields, and an MBR type byte; expected output is computed independently from those bytes and the documented value/export/default formats. Bash type/help contracts use the documented source documentation.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and documented help text (metadata only).
Documented regular-file probe behavior for independently encoded ext2 LABEL/UUID/TYPE, FAT LABEL/UUID/TYPE, and MBR PTTYPE.
Value, filtered export, default, and multiple-operand output contracts.
Label/UUID lookup restricted to explicit regular-file operands, including no match.
exclusions: GNU blkid was unavailable in the runner reference PATH; these are contract checks, not parity comparisons.
No real block device is opened or probed; fixtures are relative regular files in the runner private tree.
No-operand /sys enumeration and -L/-U discovery need a controlled device namespace or mock and are deferred.
No unmatched-device or missing-file exit-status assertion is made without the GNU oracle.
Only ext2, VFAT, and an MBR signature are covered; other filesystem and GPT signatures, parent-disk GPT partition metadata, and the complete util-linux option surface are not covered.

cases.purpose: Bash metadata contract: the selected command is registered as a builtin, without invoking its probe operation.
Bash help exposes the description documented by the pinned loadable source; no device operation is invoked.
Probe an independently encoded ext2 superblock and compare the documented value output for TYPE, LABEL, and canonical UUID.
cases.script:
zeros() {
  local n=$1
  while (( n >= 256 )); do
    printf '\0%.0s' {1..256}
    n=$((n - 256))
  done
  while (( n > 0 )); do
    printf '\0'
    n=$((n - 1))
  done
}
: > ext.img
zeros 1024 >> ext.img
printf '\x10\x00\x00\x00\x40\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x3c\x00\x00\x00\x0e\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x40\x00\x00\x00\x40\x00\x00\x00\x10\x00\x00\x00' >> ext.img
zeros 12 >> ext.img
printf '\x53\xef\x01\x00\x01\x00' >> ext.img
zeros 14 >> ext.img
printf '\x01\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x0b\x00\x00\x00\x80\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x03\x00\x00\x00' >> ext.img
printf '\x01\x23\x45\x67\x89\xab\xcd\xef\x10\x32\x54\x76\x98\xba\xdc\xfe' >> ext.img
printf 'FIXTURE_EXT     ' >> ext.img
zeros 64376 >> ext.img
blkid -s TYPE -o value ext.img
blkid -s LABEL -o value ext.img
blkid -s UUID -o value ext.img

cases.purpose: A format outside the documented default/value/export set is a Bash builtin usage error; assert the conventional usage status and that no data is printed.
No-operand enumeration and -L/-U discovery are core operations that cannot be compared safely against ambient device state.
cases.reason: Discovery needs real block devices with known signatures. uid 2000 with setgroups([]) cannot open /dev/loop-control or /dev/loopN (root:disk 0660), cannot mknod block nodes (CAP_MKNOD; device nodes are refused inside user namespaces), and the real virtio disk nodes are root:disk 0660, so no block device with known contents is visible to an unprivileged fixture. The util-linux reference cannot use the candidate-only override variables, so byte parity needs driver-provisioned devices; only the candidate-side contract (r4) is reachable unprivileged.
